topline.text: A quiet national day - today's one firm development is procedural: the 2026-27 teacher Pay Order was laid in Parliament on 16 October, starting a 21-day 'praying period' that runs to 6 November before arrears can follow.

Locally, Sheffield City Council's finance and performance committee votes today on £602k of government funding for a Firth Park Academy expansion adding three SEND rooms and 30 extra Year 7 places, alongside a temporary Parkwood Academy expansion.
topline.action: Worth a line to SLT if either school is a feeder or partner.

topline.text: A reminder: Sheffield schools break for autumn half term next week (26-30 October).

diary.text: Sheffield City Council finance and performance committee votes on £602k funding for the Firth Park Academy SEND-places expansion.
21-day parliamentary 'praying period' ends for the 2026-27 teacher Pay Order.

items.lede: Firth Park and Parkwood set for expansion.
items.body: Sheffield's finance and performance committee meets today to approve passing £602,000 of government funding to Lift Schools, part of a £701,312 scheme giving Firth Park Academy three SEND rooms, refurbished creative-arts space and upgraded science labs - raising its admission number from 240 to 270. A temporary expansion at Parkwood Academy is bundled into the same paper, both aimed at a projected Year 7 places shortfall in 2027/28 and 2028/29.

items.lede: Pay Order laid, praying period now running.
items.body: The STPCD 2026-27 Teachers' Pay Order was laid in Parliament on 16 October, confirming the 3.5% uplift (5% at the bottom of the unqualified range), backdated to 1 September. MPs now have a 21-day 'praying period' to raise objections, ending 6 November - in practice this has never been exercised, so arrears should follow once it lapses.

box.label: Jargon-buster - Praying period
box.intro: Cropping up in today's pay story:
box.text: The 21 sitting days after a statutory instrument (like the Teachers' Pay Order) is laid in Parliament, during which an MP can table a motion against it. Rarely used, but it's why pay orders aren't final the day they're laid.
